source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
Goal and rationale of the System of Rice Intensification (SRI): rice is not an aquatic plant by nature and its roots need alternating conditions of wetting and drying with adequate access to air, rather than being kept continuously flooded. When grown under SRI methods, rice plants receive sufficient nutrients and can reach a higher share of their genetic yield potential.

Under continuous flooding, rice roots are stressed and cannot develop to their natural potential. SRI practices help keep roots healthy because the plants have ample nutrients and oxygen/air available in the root zone, allowing the crop to better express its full genetic potential.

Stated benefits of SRI cited on the source slides: farmers can raise yield by roughly 2 to 3 times compared to their usual (conventional) yield. Farmers also save money because SRI requires less seed, less fertilizer, less pesticide, and less irrigation water than conventional flooded rice cultivation.

General targets/objectives mentioned for SRI seed and seedling quality: seed used should be pure and clean, evenly sprouted; the seedbed area should be well drained; seedlings should be of an improved/good variety; and seedlings should be planted while still young, at the early tillering stage, rather than left to grow old before transplanting.
